$comment: standalone-ra-account-v1 fixtures. Each case is the resolved child-only environment snapshot a producer (the Jawaka launcher daemon) exports to one authorized standalone emulator process after fork(), plus how a consumer (an emulator's native account adapter) must classify it. validate_fixtures.py classifies every case independently. The normative text is docs/standalone-ra-account.md; if this file and that page disagree, the page wins.

cases.name: unmanaged-no-handoff
cases.note: No UMRK_RA_ACCOUNT_* variable is set at all: the target is not authorized, the launcher does not implement the contract, or the launch predates it. The consumer keeps its native account behavior.

cases.name: configured-basic
cases.note: First saved account, revision 1.

cases.name: configured-punctuation
cases.note: Quotes, spaces, shell metacharacters, commas and semicolons are valid handoff data. A consumer must copy them as opaque bytes; nothing about the snapshot is shell-expanded or quoted by either side.

cases.name: configured-utf8-boundary
cases.note: The limits are UTF-8 BYTES, not characters: this username is 32 characters and exactly 63 bytes (31 latin small e with acute + 'x'), the password is 64 characters and exactly 127 bytes (63 e-acute + 'x'). Both are at the inclusive ceiling.

cases.name: signed-out-retained-revision
cases.note: The user signed out in the launcher: credentials are gone but revision 6 is retained. The consumer must clear its managed credentials and record the sign-out revision so a later lost marker cannot revive the old account.

cases.name: never-configured
cases.note: The launcher was never given an account. The consumer preserves an independently configured native emulator account only when no managed marker exists.

cases.name: invalid-account-state-passthrough
cases.note: The launcher found malformed legacy values in its database and reports that verdict: this is a valid HANDOFF carrying state invalid. A consumer disables managed authentication for the session, shows a correction message, and retains durable data for repair -- invalid is not sign-out.

cases.name: unreadable-account-source
cases.note: The launcher's database could not be read. Like invalid, this must not be mistaken for sign-out or unreadable-as-empty: durable consumer state survives the session.

cases.name: signed-out-revision-ceiling
cases.note: The revision ceiling 2^62 is inclusive. A save that would exceed it fails rather than wrapping, so this is the largest value a consumer ever sees.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-other-vars-without-version
cases.note: UMRK_RA_ACCOUNT_STATE is present but UMRK_RA_ACCOUNT_VERSION is absent. Only the TOTAL absence of every contract variable is unmanaged; a partial snapshot is a malformed handoff.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-version-two
cases.note: Version 2 does not exist yet and is refused, never guessed at.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-missing-state
cases.note: VERSION without STATE carries no verdict; a consumer cannot pick a transition from it.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-unknown-state
cases.note: Only configured, never-configured, signed-out, invalid and unreadable are defined. A fourth spelling of signed-out is a bug, not a synonym.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-credentials-on-signed-out
cases.note: Credentials present while the state is not configured. Accepting them would make a signed-out account silently playable again.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-configured-missing-username
cases.note: A configured state must carry the complete pair.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-configured-missing-password
cases.note: A configured state must carry the complete pair.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-empty-credential
cases.note: An empty username under state configured is an incomplete pair persisted by a pre-contract producer; the handoff declares it unusable instead of letting a consumer authenticate the empty string.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-username-oversized
cases.note: 64 UTF-8 bytes. The limit is 63 bytes excluding NUL; a truncated legacy DB value must be reported as invalid, never silently authenticated.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-password-oversized
cases.note: 128 UTF-8 bytes. The limit is 127 bytes excluding NUL.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-embedded-control-character
cases.note: Embedded NUL, CR or LF must be rejected anywhere in either credential: they cannot survive the producer's storage and env paths intact, so their presence means corruption.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-credential-not-utf8
cases.note: Byte 0xFF is not valid UTF-8. Fixtures express byte-exact environments through env_b64, base64 per variable, because JSON strings cannot carry invalid UTF-8.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-revision-missing
cases.note: State configured without a revision. Accepting it would let replayed credentials masquerade as the current account.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-revision-not-positive
cases.note: Zero, negative, fractional or non-numeric revisions are malformed; the producer never emits one and a consumer must not compare against one.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-revision-non-numeric
cases.note: A signed revision. strtoll, std::stoll and Python int() all accept '+7' as 7; a consumer built on one of them would accept a value the producer can never emit. A revision is one or more ASCII digits and nothing else: no sign, no whitespace, no decimal point.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-revision-overflow
cases.note: One past the 2^62 ceiling. The producer fails such a save rather than wrapping; a consumer rejects the value instead of clamping it.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-revision-on-never-configured
cases.note: A revision on a state that cannot have one (never-configured, invalid, unreadable). A retained sign-out revision is the only credential-less state that carries one.

cases.name: invalid-handoff-retroarch-credentials-leaked
cases.note: JAWAKA_CHEEVOS_* belongs to the RetroArch per-launch config handoff and must never reach a standalone child; its presence here means the producer forgot to scrub inherited state after fork.
